subject: Physics
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate, never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic while practice support is routed separately.

rungs.aha: Work measures the component of force along the actual displacement: a perpendicular force can be large and still do zero work.
learner_owns: Can identify a force direction and trace an object's displacement path.
must_contain: A force arrow and a directed path shown at several relative angles.
A zero-work case where force and displacement are perpendicular.

misconception.wrong_idea: Any force acting on a moving object does positive work because the object moves.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A mass moves in a circle while a force points toward the centre. Does that inward force do work along the instantaneous tangential displacement?
misconception.repair: Compare the force direction with the actual displacement direction; only the along-path component contributes to work.

rungs.closure: Given several force/displacement orientations, classify work as positive, negative, or zero and justify from direction.

controlled_variation.vary: the angle between a fixed-magnitude force and displacement
controlled_variation.notice: work changes from positive to zero to negative as the along-path component changes

controlled_variation.vary: the force magnitude while it remains perpendicular to displacement
controlled_variation.notice: work remains zero even as the force arrow grows

rungs.aha: Net work is the change in kinetic energy, so the sign of net work tells whether kinetic energy increases or decreases.
learner_owns: Work measures the component of force along the actual displacement: a perpendicular force can be large and still do zero work.
must_contain: Two motions with the same initial speed but opposite signs of net work.
A before/after speed comparison tied to the sign of net work rather than to one named force.

misconception.wrong_idea: Only a positive force magnitude can increase kinetic energy; negative work cannot be represented physically.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A braking force acts opposite the motion. What sign is its work, and what should happen to kinetic energy?
misconception.repair: Add the work of all acting forces to obtain net work, then match its sign and amount to the kinetic-energy change.

rungs.closure: Given initial and final speeds or a stated net work, determine the sign of the kinetic-energy change and cross-check the two descriptions.

controlled_variation.vary: the direction of the net force relative to motion
controlled_variation.hold: the initial speed and displacement length
controlled_variation.notice: positive, zero, and negative net work correspond to increasing, unchanged, and decreasing kinetic energy

rungs.aha: Potential energy is an accounting device for conservative interactions: its change replaces the work of that interaction, while dissipative forces must remain explicit work terms.
learner_owns: Net work is the change in kinetic energy, so the sign of net work tells whether kinetic energy increases or decreases.
must_contain: Two different paths between the same height endpoints for a conservative interaction.
A contrasting dissipative interaction whose work depends on path length.

misconception.wrong_idea: Every force can be assigned a potential energy so that its work can be hidden inside U.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Can kinetic friction be represented by a single potential-energy difference that depends only on the start and finish positions?
misconception.repair: Use potential energy only for conservative interactions whose work is captured by endpoint state change; keep dissipative work explicit.

rungs.closure: For a set of forces, identify which may be represented by potential-energy changes and which must remain explicit work terms.

controlled_variation.vary: the path between the same two heights
controlled_variation.notice: the gravitational potential-energy change is the same for both paths

controlled_variation.vary: the path length between comparable endpoints
controlled_variation.notice: frictional work changes with path length and cannot be encoded by endpoints alone

rungs.aha: Mechanical energy K + U is conserved only when non-conservative and unmodelled external work vanish; friction or a moving support changes the energy account.
learner_owns: Potential energy is an accounting device for conservative interactions: its change replaces the work of that interaction, while dissipative forces must remain explicit work terms.
must_contain: A frictionless descent compared with an otherwise identical rough descent.
An explicit system boundary and every external/non-conservative work term before K + U is compared.

misconception.wrong_idea: Mechanical energy is always conserved, so one may write Ki + Ui = Kf + Uf even when friction or a moving support does work.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: A block slides down a rough ramp. If it starts from the same height as on a smooth ramp, must it reach the bottom with the same kinetic energy?
misconception.repair: Check for non-conservative and external work first; use K + U conservation only when those net work terms vanish, otherwise include them in the balance.

rungs.closure: Given an energy-accounting problem, state whether mechanical energy is conserved and write the correct balance including any non-conservative or external work.

controlled_variation.vary: the starting height on a frictionless track
controlled_variation.hold: the same system boundary and no non-conservative work
controlled_variation.notice: lost potential energy reappears as kinetic energy and K + U stays constant

controlled_variation.vary: the surface from frictionless to rough
controlled_variation.notice: K + U for the mechanical degrees of freedom decreases by the negative friction work

rungs.aha: Power is the rate of doing work: average power uses total work over an interval, while instantaneous power depends on force and velocity at that instant.
learner_owns: Mechanical energy K + U is conserved only when non-conservative and unmodelled external work vanish; friction or a moving support changes the energy account.
must_contain: Two machines doing the same total work in different times.
A changing-speed case where the same average power hides different instantaneous rates.

misconception.wrong_idea: If two processes do the same total work, they necessarily have the same power.
misconception.diagnostic_prompt: Two motors lift the same load through the same height, one in half the time. Do they do the same work, and do they have the same average power?
misconception.repair: Separate amount of work from rate: average power divides total work by elapsed time; instantaneous power depends on what is happening at that instant.

rungs.closure: Given work and timing information, distinguish total work, average power, and when enough information exists to discuss instantaneous power.

controlled_variation.vary: the time taken to perform the same work
controlled_variation.hold: the load, displacement, and total work
controlled_variation.notice: average power changes while work does not

controlled_variation.vary: the speed during different moments of one process
controlled_variation.hold: the applied force direction and one overall interval
controlled_variation.notice: the instantaneous power can vary even when one average power describes the interval

family.invariant_demand: Choose the system and actual path, identify work contributions and any legitimate potential-energy terms, decide whether mechanical-energy conservation applies, and use the resulting energy account or power relation without dropping signs.
family.difficult_move: Deciding which interactions belong in potential energy and which must remain explicit work, because that decision determines whether K + U may be treated as conserved.
family.independent_check: All energy terms must share units and signs, the final energy-account residual must close to zero, and any zero-work claim must agree with the force/displacement geometry.

support_ladder.handed_over: The system boundary and a classification of the named interactions as conservative or explicit-work terms are supplied.
The system boundary and actual path are supplied.
Only the physical situation and requested energy or power quantity are supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: A rough track replaces a frictionless one and the learner must decide whether simple mechanical-energy conservation still applies.
A force-and-path diagram must be translated into signed work contributions before an energy balance can be written.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which force components are along the actual displacement

transfer.changed_demand: A moving support does work through its contact force, so the learner must include that external transfer before solving for the final kinetic energy.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether the contact point itself moves along the force direction

transfer.changed_demand: Two machines perform the same task with different time profiles and the learner must separate total work from average and instantaneous power.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which reported rate is tied to the whole interval rather than a single instant
